fields.value: Enable shared GPU batch inference on Apple Silicon (MPS) hosts

## Problem

In `src/etude/eval/resources.py` (`_has_gpu`, lines 105–118), Etude only detects GPUs by calling `nvidia-smi`. On owned Apple Silicon Macs (e.g., `mini-r2`, 8 cores, 16 GiB unified RAM), `_has_gpu()` returns `False`, so `divide_cpus` sets `shared = False` (`threads = 0`) and never starts the shared batching agent process (`running_agents`). Every game worker falls back to loading its own CPU copy of each checkpoint and running `batch=1` with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, leaving the Apple Silicon GPU 100% idle.

In `tla_trophies_colab_500k_v2`, 68,836 held-out games on `mini-r2` took 20+ hours on CPU `batch=1` because of this.

## Outcome

- Etude detects Apple Silicon MPS hosts cleanly (without importing Torch in the parent process, e.g., macOS `arm64` / Metal device check or an opt-in/auto accelerator probe) and starts the shared `running_agents` batching process just like on CUDA hosts.
- `divide_cpus` sizes `games` and `threads` sensibly for unified-memory Macs (respecting `memory_gb` and physical RAM without over-allocating game processes or starving MPS).
- Companion `manabot` task `MTG-497` selects `mps` (and `bf16` where supported) in `manabot/eval/agent_loader.py` and sends multi-row batches per pairing.
- Measured speedup on an Apple Silicon Mac (games/hr and batch sizes via `batches.json`) over CPU `batch=1` on a real Manabot checkpoint (`w160l8`).

## Constraints & overlap

- Keep the parent and game processes framework-free (never import Torch in `etude.eval.resources`).
- Coordinates with `EXP-77` (GPU saturation on CUDA/4090/H100) and `manabot` `MTG-497` (MPS + `bf16` + concurrent 4-game pairings in `manabot/eval/agent_loader.py`).
